outcome_evidence: This is a provisional window outcome: sorting is not completed, and later context is absent. wrist_cam shows the carrot deposited alongside the pink animal toy in the purple bowl at frames 473–477, mixing the two categories. overhead_cam shows other objects still on the table at frame 699. Repeated finger closures near the blue toy do not visibly acquire it. At frames 350–369 the empty gripper opens before approaching the carrot; the supplied context does not establish continued failing actions from the previously reported brown-object attempt.

failure_annotations.explanation: The robot releases the carrot into the purple bowl at frames 472–476, where wrist_cam clearly shows the pink animal toy already lying. overhead_cam confirms the deposit and withdrawal. Although the physical transfer succeeds, placing food and a toy together contradicts separation into two bowls; the failure interval ends when the robot starts moving toward the remaining objects.
failure_annotations.recovery: Assign one bowl to food and the other to toys, then transfer the carrot or the pink toy to the appropriate separate bowl; no human intervention is visibly necessary.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The objects rest inside the bowl without visible damage; the consequence is incorrect sorting rather than a demonstrated damage hazard.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: Both misplaced-category objects remain accessible in an upright bowl and can be rearranged by the robot without human resetting.

failure_annotations.recovery: Open and lift clear of the toy, reassess its displaced position, and align the fingers around a graspable portion of its body before retrying; avoid the nearby brown and orange objects. No human intervention is visibly required.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The toy is displaced locally but remains on the table; neither camera establishes damage or a meaningful damage risk.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The toy and neighboring objects remain accessible in a usable workspace, allowing a revised grasp without environmental repair or human intervention.
